overview: The Maldives is an island country in the Indian Ocean, south-west of India. Its capital, Malé, is one of the most densely populated cities in the world. The Maldives became independent from British protection in 1965. Tourism, especially resorts on their own private islands, is the biggest part of its economy.

geography.text: The Maldives is made up of around 1,200 coral islands grouped into 26 atolls. It is the lowest-lying country in the world, with most land only about a metre above sea level, which makes it very vulnerable to rising seas. Its coral reefs and lagoons are famous for their marine life.

history.text: The Maldives was Buddhist for centuries before converting to Islam in 1153. It was a sultanate for more than 800 years, at times under Portuguese occupation and later under British protection. The Maldives became independent in 1965 and a republic in 1968. The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami caused major damage.

events.title: Portuguese occupation
events.text: The Portuguese occupy Malé for about fifteen years.

events.title: British protectorate
events.text: The Maldives comes under British protection.

events.title: Tsunami
events.text: The Indian Ocean tsunami floods many islands.
